column1: # Golden vectors for coordinate coarsening.
# WHY BIT-EXACT
# The same coordinate is coarsened in four places that must agree exactly:
#   services/job/internal/domain/geo.go      (CoarsenPoint)
#   services/user/internal/domain/geo.go     (CoarsenPoint)
#   database/cmd/encrypt-pii/geo.go          (coarsenPoint — unexported CLI copy)
#   database/migrations/104_*.up.sql         (pii_coarsen_ordinate)
# Go cannot share an internal package across module boundaries
# separate implementations kept in agreement by hand. Drift does not fail
# loudly: it snaps a point into a NEIGHBOURING grid cell
# listing quietly missing from a radius search
# privacy invariant breaking. Nobody gets an error.
# The residue is the trap. math.Round(v/0.01)*0.01 leaves a binary residue —
# -97.74 becomes -97.74000000000001 — which looks like a bug and is not.
# "Cleaning it up" by re-rounding is exactly what breaks bit-equality with
# Postgres
